## Observed Facts

Data Scope: BGL dataset, level = FATAL, all time, no component or text filter.

The BGL FATAL Log Entries total 855,195 [E1], spread over 8 months from June 2005 to January 2006:

| Month | FATAL Log Entries |
|---|---|
| 2005-06 | 548,475 [E1] |
| 2005-07 | 19,769 [E1] |
| 2005-08 | 69,452 [E1] |
| 2005-09 | 81,818 [E1] |
| 2005-10 | 42,542 [E1] |
| 2005-11 | 47,641 [E1] |
| 2005-12 | 44,859 [E1] |
| 2006-01 | 639 [E1] |

- June 2005 is the largest month by far, with 548,475 Log Entries [E1]. That is about 64% of all FATAL Log Entries in the period (548,475 / 855,195, my calculation from [E1]).
- After June, the count falls to 19,769 in July [E1], then rises to a second peak of 81,818 in September [E1]. It stays in the 42,000–70,000 range for August, October, November and December [E1].
- January 2006 drops to 639 Log Entries [E1].

## Hypotheses

- The June 2005 volume looks like a one-off burst rather than steady recurrence. A small number of very chatty sources may account for most of it, though I have not checked this.
- The January 2006 drop may reflect the end of the data capture rather than an improvement, since the period is cut off there. The first and last months may be partial.

## Unknowns

- Which Components produced the June 2005 burst. The month trend does not split by component.
- Whether June 2005 and January 2006 are full or partial months. I have not checked the corpus time range with `describe_corpus`.
- Whether the same Components drive the July–December pattern. This needs a component breakdown.
- Whether the monthly counts reflect real fault activity or logging behaviour. The logs cannot tell these apart by themselves.

## Next Step

Run a component breakdown for the June 2005 month to see which Components drive the burst. Then compare the same breakdown for September 2005 to see whether the second peak involves the same Components.
